judgments.rationale: Frames explanations as proposals for criticism, emphasizes novel expectations and predictions written before tests, and treats unexpected results as opportunities for correction.
Prioritizes rival accounts producing discriminating predictions; fitting previous observations is insufficient, and successful prediction leaves criticism open.
Begins with a concrete moving-pattern distinction, rejects the manual label as understanding, and asks what physically produces successive flashes through a reversible intervention.

Organizes explanation around an explicit proposal and its potentially adverse test, ending by restricting the conclusion to the specific account tested. Shares substantial concrete pedagogy with Feynman.
Pairs experimental discrimination with human susceptibility to prestige and persuasion, then makes public participation and the accessibility of earned knowledge central.
Demands a physical push-or-pull mechanism beneath elegant language, tracks practical disturbances and drift, and explains the next trial through observable differences.

The strongest evidence is the distinction between naming and understanding and the conversion of an impressive phrase into a concrete causal question. The stadium analogy and polished public explanatory register could also support Sagan; experimental content alone does not discriminate them well.

Starts by asking what darkness physically consists of, develops tactile comparisons and practical precautions, and uses partial answers to generate progressively more specific mechanisms to investigate.
Translates the technical name into an imaginable neighboring-bulb mechanism, identifies sequence and delay as the useful measurements, and separates apparent travel from a transmitted influence.
Turns vague equilibrium language into direction, amount and timing, insists the original effect be reproducible, and stresses scrutiny of favorable evidence as much as awkward evidence.

Connects a modest everyday mystery with the dignity and pleasure of broader inquiry, combines multiple natural explanations with patient observations, and ends by emphasizing the world becoming readable.
Replaces a vague mystery with questions one can watch happen, distinguishes visible coating from its causal history, and makes comparative trials lead to further physically workable questions.
